subject: Business Models
title: Indirect Network Effects
description: A short lesson to help you apply Indirect Network Effects.

hook.text: More iPhone users attract more app developers. More apps attract more iPhone users. A virtuous cycle.

buildup.text: Indirect network effects happen across sides: one side's growth benefits the other side.

discovery.text: Windows dominated PCs because it had the most software. Developers built for Windows because it had the most users.

twist.text: Indirect effects can reverse too. As developers left BlackBerry, users followed. The spiral went negative.

climax.text: Indirect network effects explain why platform battles are winner-take-most. The loop reinforces itself.

punchline.text: Users attract developers, developers attract users. The loop decides.

quiz.question: What are indirect network effects?
options: Growth on one side benefits the other side

details.summary: Indirect network effects occur when growth in one user group increases the platform's value for a different user group. More riders on Uber attract more drivers, which reduces wait times, attracting even more riders in a virtuous cycle across the two sides of the market.
details.whyItMatters: Indirect network effects are the engine of multi-sided platforms. Understanding how to ignite and sustain cross-side value creation is essential for building marketplace businesses from ride-sharing to app stores.
takeaways: Growth on one side of a platform attracts users on the other side
Cross-side effects create virtuous cycles that accelerate platform growth
Balancing both sides of the market is critical for platform success

faq.question: How do indirect network effects differ from direct ones?
faq.answer: Direct effects mean same-side users benefit from each other, like phone users calling each other. Indirect effects mean one side benefits from growth on the other side, like app developers benefiting from more iPhone users and vice versa.

faq.question: What is the chicken-and-egg problem in indirect network effects?
faq.answer: New platforms need supply to attract demand, but supply won't come without demand. Solutions include subsidizing one side, seeding supply through partnerships, starting with a single-player value proposition, or launching in a focused geographic niche.
